text:
micah: Heads up — smallbatch latency regressed ~18-25% on the canary fleet after yesterday's CUDA 12.12p1 + triton/opscheduler merge. CI smallbatch perf test failed 3/3 runs.

linda: Saw the same in the nightly smoke. 90th and 99th both moved up, throughput stable. This looks like more queuing/blocking than math perf.

oliver: I ran a quick bisect across the last two merges. Repro narrows to tricore/triton#842 (opscheduler preemption change) + driver 12.12p1. If I roll back the triton opscheduler change on our staging image the smallbatch numbers return to baseline.

sarah: Nsight capture on a repro run: a couple kernels (matmul_32x128_f16 and attention_fwd_fp16) are waiting on a host-to-device stream that’s being preempted by a background copy. Looks like stream priorities got inverted under the new scheduler hint logic.

micah: Paste of the critical part of the Nsight timeline (trimmed):
```
0.000 - kernel A (stream 1, high) queued
0.001 - h2d copy (stream 7, medium) scheduled and runs, preempts kernel A
0.003 - kernel A resumes after 2ms gap -> adds ~1.8ms wall
0.004 - kernel B queued -> more queuing
```

oliver: Perf flame summary (local run):
- baseline smallbatch 95th: 12.4ms
- canary smallbatch 95th: 15.1ms
- delta concentrated on kernel latency + scheduling stalls

perf-bot: CI perf artifact: https://ci.redwood.dev/artefacts/1733334444/smallbatch-run-logs
ci-bot: smallbatch perf-checker: FAILED (regression > 10%). Full diff: https://ci.redwood.dev/diffs/1733334444

linda: I also grabbed a short trace of CUDA profiling counters. SM occupancy and achieved occupancy look normal. But there are repeated gaps labeled "stream-preempt" in the timeline.

omments: @oliver can you share the git bisect range and the offending commit hash? We should decide revert vs. mitigation.

oliver: Bisect range: HEAD~12..HEAD. Offender: tricore/triton@c5b9a7e (opscheduler: prefer_preempt=true change + priority hint). When I flip prefer_preempt back to false locally, scheduling behavior matches baseline.

sarah: We also confirmed that if we downgrade driver from 12.12p1 -> 12.12 (previous) with the new triton merge, the regression is reduced but not fully gone. So it's an interaction: driver subtly changed preemption semantics and triton change nudged workloads into the new corner case.

micah: Action proposal: hold the rollout for the triton opscheduler change on canary, add a temporary config flag in our runtime to set prefer_preempt=false by default for smallbatch profiles, and open a ticket with triton and NVIDIA driver SRE.

linda: Agreed. I opened a rollout hold flag on the canary groups (hold_id: hold-2026-03-18-sched). Can we get a quick PR that sets prefer_preempt=false for the smallbatch batcher config?

oliver: Will do. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4512 — sets prefer_preempt=false for batch_size <= 8 and adds telemetry when preemption stalls exceed 0.5ms per request.

micah: For the triage notes:
- Root cause hypothesis: opscheduler preemption hint + driver 12.12p1 changed preemption timing -> priority inversion for small, latency-sensitive batches.
- Short-term fix: rollout hold + runtime config toggle (prefer_preempt=false) for smallbatch profiles.
- Mid-term: upstream conversation with triton to make default more conservative and add a gate for small-latency SLOs.
- Long-term: add a targeted CI smoke that runs canary smallbatch with driver 12.12p1 + opscheduler changes under instrumentation.

sarah: I've attached the raw nvprof capture and a small python repro script in the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENGRT-1729

micah: Assigning owners: oliver -> PR and revert plan if needed, linda -> rollout hold and canary monitoring, sarah -> driver/Triton escalation + Nsight artifacts, micah -> cross-team comms and release notes.

linda: Quick note — telemetry shows customer-facing p95 increase on a small subset of dedicated nodes that match the canary image. We should proactively notify SRE & support if rollout stays held longer than an hour. :bell:

perf-bot: new perf-check baseline created for canary branch: https://ci.redwood.dev/baselines/1733334444

micah: Thanks team. Let's aim to get the runtime toggle PR merged and canary re-run within 2 hours. If PR doesn't clear perf gate, we revert the triton merge.

oliver: PR up, link again: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4512 — requesting urgent review.

sarah: I'll start the NVIDIA driver ticket, attaching the trimmed Nsight timeline and indicating priority "high — regression impact on latency SLOs".

linda: tagging @support and @sre so they can watch the canary set: @support @sre

micah: I'll post a brief runbook summary after we verify the small toggle effect.
